result.title: From Memory Hits to Answerable Evidence: Query-Conditioned Memory Compilation for Long-Term Agent Memory
result.summary: Long-term agent memory requires recovering answer-relevant evidence dispersed across turns and sessions. Existing systems increasingly use structured memories and adaptive retrieval, yet often pass retrieved or expanded units directly to the reader, coupling memory addressing with evidence presentation and leaving the final context redundant or incomplete. To address this gap, we propose MemCompile, a query-conditioned evidence compilation framework for long-term conversational memory. Given a query, the Address Plane locates relevant support through compact source-linked descriptors and capacity-aware Cells, while a normalization boundary resolves heterogeneous retrieval hits to stable SourcePacket identities. Its Evidence Plane then allocates a bounded evidence budget across complementary packets, admits limited additional support, and renders the retained claims associated with each selected packet into an answer-ready context. MemCompile achieves 80.52% Judge Accuracy on LoCoMo and extends the empirical quality-cost Pareto frontier to a higher-quality regime. Its strong performance on LongMemEval-S further suggests that the benefits of query-conditioned compilation generalize across long-term conversational-memory benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MemCompile：给定查询后，先用地址平面把分散于多轮对话的检索命中归一化为稳定的 SourcePacket，再在证据平面按有界预算筛选互补证据并渲染成可直接作答的上下文，在 LoCoMo 与 LongMemEval-S 上验证效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 属长期对话记忆的文本检索/证据编译，与 LVR 无直接关系；其「有界证据预算 + 互补支持筛选」的编译思路或可启发 VLM 推理中的视觉证据筛选与取证、停止决策，属较远领域可供核查的借鉴线索。
